eras.title: Founding and the Roadster
eras.intro: Tesla Motors was incorporated in 2003, and Elon Musk led its first funding round in 2004. The first Roadster reached a customer in 2008, followed by a government loan, a 2010 stock market debut and the purchase of the Fremont factory.

eras.title: Model S, Model X and the first Gigafactory
eras.intro: Model S deliveries began in 2012 and the car collected top awards and safety ratings. Tesla launched its Supercharger network, repaid its government loan early, broke ground on a Nevada battery Gigafactory and switched on Autopilot by software update. Model X deliveries began in 2015.

eras.title: Model 3 and production hell
eras.intro: The $35,000 Model 3 was unveiled in 2016, and Tesla struggled through 2018 to reach 5,000 a week. The same years brought SolarCity, the "funding secured" tweets and SEC settlement, a first profitable quarter, and the Semi, Model Y and Cybertruck unveilings.

eras.title: Going global: Shanghai, Berlin and Texas
eras.intro: China-built Model 3s reached buyers in 2020, and new Gigafactories opened in Berlin and Texas in 2022. Tesla posted its first profitable year, joined the S&P 500 and began a limited FSD Beta, while regulators stepped up scrutiny of Autopilot.

eras.title: Price cuts, a charging standard and the AI turn
eras.intro: Tesla cut prices in 2023 as rival automakers adopted its charging plug. Cybertruck deliveries began, FSD moved to end-to-end AI, and Autopilot was recalled on about 2 million cars. Tesla also became a Texas corporation and unveiled Cybercab in 2024.

eras.title: Robotaxi, Cybercab and Optimus
eras.intro: Robotaxi service launched in Austin in 2025 and spread to more cities, and paid Cybercab rides began in Austin in 2026. Model S and X production ended to make room for Optimus, Semi volume production began, and many promises remain open.
